cases.title: a public NAME that resolves to a private address
cases.notes: The bypass a URL-string check misses entirely: the attacker owns the DNS record, so the host looks public and the connection is internal. A port that validates only the literal passes every row above this one and fails here.

cases.title: a name answering with one public and one private address
cases.notes: EVERY resolved address is checked, not the first. A host answering with both reaches the private one, and a port that stops at the first record reads this as public.

cases.title: a public host redirecting into the metadata endpoint
cases.notes: A DIFFERENT code from the address refusals, and deliberately so: the caller's input was fine and the server aimed them somewhere internal. Redirects are followed by default in every HTTP client here, so a port that validates only the URL it was handed makes the internal request and never knows.

cases.title: the UNGUARDED fetch still fetches a loopback address
cases.notes: PHP and TypeScript preserve their pre-existing unguarded fetch methods. Python has no unguarded media fetch by design and skips this legacy-path control; adding one would introduce an SSRF-capable path solely to make the corpus greener.

cases.title: a non-http scheme
cases.notes: Handed to an HTTP client that would happily read the file. Refused before any address check, because there is no address to check.

cases.title: a host that resolves to nothing
cases.notes: An empty answer must mean "could not be verified", never "nothing to check". A port that treats no records as a pass turns every DNS failure into an allowed fetch.

cases.title: a public host redirecting forever
cases.notes: Six requests pin the default redirect-hop allowance at five in PHP, TypeScript and Python: the initial request plus five allowed hops are sent, then too_many_redirects must be raised before a seventh request. A language that defaults to three would refuse under the same code but fail this six-request assertion. Every response redirects even when already at redirects_to; no hop serves content.
